questions.q: Why does the summary recommend specializing in a single service?
a: It builds expertise and a reputation that draws clients
It lets you meet every need a client might have
It makes the business harder for buyers to value
It allows you to charge lower prices than rivals
questions.why: Lesson 1 says focus makes you the known expert, which brings referrals and makes higher prices easier to negotiate.

questions.q: What should a founder do early to prepare a company for sale?
a: Delegate so the business can run without them
Personally handle every client relationship
Keep all financial decisions to themselves
Avoid hiring until the sale is complete
questions.why: Lesson 2 warns against becoming the linchpin and advises handing off responsibilities as early as possible.

questions.q: What happens when the founder becomes indispensable to the company?
a: Growth stalls because everything depends on their schedule
Clients become more loyal to the brand
The company sells for a higher price
Employees take on more responsibility
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that a founder stuck in every decision has no time to grow the business or take a vacation.

questions.q: Why is one big client dangerous for cash flow?
a: A late payment can leave you unable to cover payroll
It forces you to lower your quality standards
It makes your best employees quit immediately
It brings in too many new customers at once
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes a client worth 40% of revenue whose delayed payment threatens payroll and rent.

questions.q: Besides cash flow, what problem comes from depending on a few big clients?
a: It weakens your power to negotiate prices
It makes marketing far more expensive
It sharply raises your tax burden
It limits the range of services you offer
questions.why: Lesson 3 says you cannot raise fees or extend deadlines without risking the loss of a major customer.
